title: Approval policy fails closed across session modes
summary: Approval policy guards interactive and unattended session modes together, not only the interactive path.

protected.asset: Every action path that approval can gate
protected.failure: One session mode, typically an unattended one, bypasses the approval posture the operator believes they have.

rationale: Approval posture is only as strong as the weakest session mode. Where unattended jobs exist, they must be explicitly denied closed; where none exist, guarding the interactive mode is sufficient. Missing facts about either mode leave the decision open rather than silently safe.

variants.description: Read back the interactive mode and every unattended mode per home and compare both against the intended pair.
Additionally fail the deployment itself on any read-back mismatch, treating an unreadable value as a retryable state rather than a pass.

verification.method: Read the interactive approval mode and each unattended approval mode the build exposes, per home, and compare against the intended posture; on builds lacking an unattended mode key, record the required external execution boundary instead.
verification.evidence: Mode names, effective values and comparison outcomes per home; missing keys listed explicitly.

rollback.method: Restore previous mode values per home and record the acceptance of any permissive value.

failure_modes: Unattended modes are read from one home and assumed for all.
A missing unattended key is treated as denial instead of an open path needing an external boundary.

hermes_versions.notes: Synthetic seed control: the range is an illustrative placeholder for the example registry, not a verified compatibility claim.
